explanation: Tasman sailed for the Dutch East India Company but never landed. Dutch mapmakers named the islands after the province of Zeeland, and Tasmania honours him.

claims.text: Abel Tasman, in 1642, was the first European known to reach New Zealand.
James Cook reached New Zealand in 1769, and Magellan and Drake never reached it.
Abel Tasman sailed for the Dutch East India Company.
Tasman did not land in New Zealand.
New Zealand was named by Dutch mapmakers after the Dutch province of Zeeland.
Tasmania is named after Abel Tasman.
